en: The process of imparting knowledge, skill and judgment.
Facts, skills and ideas that have been learned, especially through formal instruction.

education.ety:
Borrowed from Middle French éducation, from Latin ēducātiō (“a breeding, bringing up, rearing”), from ēducō (“to educate, train”), from ēdūcō (“to lead forth, to take out; to raise up, to erect”). See educate.
Morphologically educate + -ion.

ex.en: You have the advantage of a good education.
ex.ja: 君にはりっぱな教育を受けたという利点がある。

ex.en: My education has made me what I am.
ex.ja: 教育のおかげで私は今日のようになった。

ex.en: Education means something more than going to school.
ex.ja: 教育とはただ学校に行くだけではなくそれ以上のことを意味する。

note.ja: e（外へ）+ duc（導く）+ ation。（才能を）引き出すこと →「教育」。

en: A final examination; a test or examination given at the end of a term or class; the test that concludes a class.
A final examination taken at the end of the final year of an undergraduate course, which contributes towards a student's degree classific…
Last; ultimate.
Conclusive; decisive.
To qualify for the final round of a competition.

final.ety: From Middle English final, fynal, fynall, from Old French final, from Latin fīnālis (“of or relating to the end or to boundaries”), from fīnis (“end”); see fine. Replaced native English endly (“final”).

ex.en: I'm busy because the finals are drawing on.
ex.ja: 期末試験が近づいているので忙しい。

ex.en: The final score of the game was 3 to 1.
ex.ja: その試合の最終得点は３対１だった。

ex.en: I'm going all out for the final week.
ex.ja: ラストの1週間死ぬ気で頑張る。

note.ja: ラテン語 finis（終わり・境界）から。fin（終わり）+ al。終わりの →「最後の・最終の」。finish（終える）、infinite（終わりのない→無限の）も同じ。

en: Previous.
The first of aforementioned two items.

former.ety: Inherited from Middle English former, comparative of forme (“first”), from Old English forma (“first”), descended from Proto-Germanic *frumô. Parallel to prior (via Latin), as comparative form from same Proto-Indo-European root. Related to first and fore (thence before), from Proto-Germanic.

ex.en: I prefer the former plan to the latter.
ex.ja: はじめの計画のほうが後のより良いと思う。

ex.en: The former captain was superior to the present one.
ex.ja: 前のキャプテンは、現在のキャプテンより優れていました。

ex.en: The former is better than the latter.
ex.ja: 後者より前者の方がいい。

note.ja: 古英語 forma（最初の）の比較級。より前の →「前の・元の・前者」。latter（後者）と対。

en: The foremost side of something or the end that faces the direction it normally moves.
The side of a building with the main entrance.
Located at or near the front.
Pronounced with the highest part of the body of the tongue toward the front of the mouth, near the hard palate (most often describing a v…
To face, be opposite to.
To face up to, to meet head-on, to confront.
Used to summon a worker on duty, such as a bellhop.

front.ety:
Etymology tree
Latin frontem
Old French frontbor.
Middle English frount
English front
From Middle English front, frunt, frount, from Old French front, frunt, from Latin frōns, frontem (“forehead”). Doublet of frons.

ex.en: The number of the front desk is No 1.
ex.ja: フロントの番号は一番です。

ex.en: The truck cut in front of my car.
ex.ja: トラックが私の前に割り込んだ。

ex.en: The troops were retired from the front lines.
ex.ja: その部隊は戦線から撤退させられた。

note.ja: ラテン語 frons（額）から。顔の前の部分 →「前面・正面・前線」。frontier（国境・最前線）も同じ。

en: A child, adolescent, or (loosely) a young adult.
A person whose childhood took place in a particular time period or area.
To dupe or deceive.
To deceive or dupe as a joke.

kid.ety: From Middle English kide, from Old Norse kið (“young goat”), from Proto-Germanic *kidją, *kittīną (“goatling, kid”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *gʰaydn-, *ǵʰaydn- (“goat”) or Proto-Indo-European *gidʰ- (“kid, goatling, little goat”). Compare Swedish and Danish kid, German Kitz and Kitze, Albanian kedh and kec. The sense of child has been in use since the 1590s as slang, and since the 1840s in informal use.

ex.en: Say, he is no more than a kid.
ex.ja: 何だ、まだほんの子供じゃないか。

ex.en: By the way, how many kids are going?
ex.ja: ところで、何人の子どもが行くのですか。

ex.en: You should build a fire under the kid.
ex.ja: お子さんに少し、発破をかけた方がいいですよ。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「子ヤギ」。子ヤギ →（くだけて）「子ども」、子ども扱いする →「からかう・冗談を言う（You're kidding!）」。

en: A strip of fabric, especially from the edge of a piece of cloth.
Material used for cloth selvage.
To create or recite a list.
To place in listings.

Cognates

* Dutch lijst (“picture frame, list”)

ex.en: Don't leave my name out of your list.
ex.ja: リストから私の名を落とさないで下さい。

ex.en: Add a few more names to the list.
ex.ja: そのリストにもう２、３の名前を加えなさい。

ex.en: Please check all the items on this list.
ex.ja: このリストの項目を全部チェックして下さい。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「縁・帯状に並んだもの」。一覧表、名簿、一覧にする。

en: Prepared for immediate action or use.
first only used predicatively, freely used from the end of the 17th century
To prepare; to make ready for action.

ready.ety: From Middle English redy, redi, rædiȝ, iredi, ȝerǣdi, alteration ( + -y) of earlier irēd, irede, ȝerād (“ready, prepared”), from Old English rǣde, ġerǣde (also ġerȳde) ("prepared, prompt, ready, ready for riding (horse), mounted (on a horse), skilled, simple, easy"), from Proto-Germanic *garaidijaz, *raidijaz, from base *raidaz (“ready”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂reh₁dʰ-, *h₂reh₁- (“to count, put in order, arrange, make comfortable”) and also probably conflated with Proto-Indo-European *reydʰ- (“to ride”) in the sense of "set to ride, able or fit to go, ready". Cognate with Scots readie, re

ex.en: I am ready to do anything for you.
ex.ja: 君のためなら喜んでなんでもする。

ex.en: We'll leave as soon as you are ready.
ex.ja: あなたの用意が出来次第出発しましょう。

ex.en: We will soon be ready for the party.
ex.ja: 間もなく、私たちのパーティーの準備ができるでしょう。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「準備が整った」。用意ができた、すぐに〜する（ready to help）。readily（すぐに・快く）。

en: On some occasions, over some periods, or in certain circumstances, but not always.

sometimes.ety: From Middle English sumtymes, somtymes, som tymes, equivalent to sometime + -s (adverbial suffix). Compare West Frisian somstiden (“sometimes”), Dutch somtijds, somwijlen (“sometimes”).

ex.en: You know, sometimes you need to hear it.
ex.ja: でもね、聞きたい時もあるのよ。

ex.en: Oh, yes. I sometimes see him on TV.
ex.ja: ああ、そうだね。時々テレビで見るよ。

ex.en: An old belief is sometimes still widely current.
ex.ja: 古い信仰が今だに広く行われていることがある。

note.ja: some（ある）+ time + -s。「ある時には」→「ときどき」。

en: One's male offspring.
A male adopted person in relation to his adoptive parents.
To produce (i.e. bear, father, beget) a son.
To address (someone) as "son".

son.ety: From Middle English sonn, sone, sun, sune, from Old English sunu (“son”), from Proto-West Germanic *sunu, from Proto-Germanic *sunuz (“son”), from Proto-Indo-European *suHnús (“son”), from Proto-Indo-European *sewH- (“to bear; give birth”).

ex.en: We had a good opinion of your son.
ex.ja: 我々は君の息子さんを立派だとおもっている。

ex.en: Mr. Young wishes his son would study harder.
ex.ja: ヤングさんは息子がもっと勉強してくれる様にと願っている。

ex.en: Why does he always run his son down?
ex.ja: なぜ彼はいつも自分の息子を悪くいうのだろうか。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「息子」。PIE *suHnús にさかのぼる古い語。

en: A paved part of road, usually in a village or a town.
A road as above, but including the sidewalks (pavements) and buildings.
To build or equip with streets.
To eject; to throw onto the streets.

ex.en: By chance, I met her in the street.
ex.ja: 偶然、私は道端で彼女に会った。

ex.en: The flower shop is just across the street.
ex.ja: 花屋はちょうど通りの向こう側だ。

ex.en: I remember seeing her once on the street.
ex.ja: 一度彼女に路上で会ったことを覚えている。

note.ja: ラテン語 strata（舗装された道）から。→「通り・街路」。stratum（層）も同じ語源。

en: To transport toward somebody/somewhere.
To supply or contribute.
The sound of a telephone ringing.

bring.ety:
From Middle English bryngen, from Old English bringan, from Proto-West Germanic *bringan, from Proto-Germanic *bringaną (“to bring”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰrenk-, possibly based on *bʰer-.
Compare Scots bring, West Frisian bringe, Low German brengen, Dutch brengen, Afrikaans bring, German bringen; also Welsh hebrwng (“to bring, lead”), Tocharian B pränk- (“to take away; restrain oneself, hold back”), Latvian brankti (“lying close”), Lithuanian branktas (“whiffletree”).

ex.en: Hard work has brought him where he is.
ex.ja: 勤勉さが今の彼をつくりあげた。

ex.en: Can't you bring down the price a bit?
ex.ja: もう少し安くならない？

ex.en: Please bring your plan up at the meeting.
ex.ja: どうぞ君の案を会議に持ち出してください。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「話し手のいる所へ持ってくる」。持ってくる（bring a friend）、もたらす（bring happiness）。take（持っていく）とは方向が逆。

en: A specialized division of a university.
An institution of higher education teaching undergraduates.

ex.en: My brother seems to enjoy himself at college.
ex.ja: 兄さんは大学で楽しそうです。

ex.en: In those days, few people went to college.
ex.ja: その頃は、ほとんどの人が大学へは行かなかった。

ex.en: This article was written by a college professor.
ex.ja: この記事はある大学教授によって書かれました。

note.ja: col（共に）+ leg（選ばれた）。ラテン語 collega（共に選ばれた仲間）から。仲間の集まり →「団体」→「大学」。colleague（同僚）も同語源。

en: The generally unidirectional movement of a gas or fluid.
The part of a fluid that moves continuously in a certain direction, especially (oceanography) ellipsis of ocean current.
Existing or occurring at the moment.
Generally accepted, used, practiced, or prevalent at the moment; having currency.

current.ety: From Middle English curraunt, borrowed from Old French curant (French courant), present participle of courre (“to run”), from Latin currere (“to run”) (present participle currens). Doublet of courant.

ex.en: An old belief is sometimes still widely current.
ex.ja: 古い信仰が今だに広く行われていることがある。

ex.en: The current king is present at the party.
ex.ja: 今の国王が会合に出席されている。

ex.en: You must take an interest in current events.
ex.ja: 今日の出来事には関心を持たなければいけません。

note.ja: cur（走る・流れる）+ rent。今流れている →「現在の・流れ・電流」。currency（流通→通貨）。

en: Something that is representative of all such things in a group.
Something that serves to illustrate or explain a rule.
To be illustrated or exemplified (by).

example.ety: From Middle English example, exaumple, from Old French example, essaumple, from Latin exemplum (“sample, pattern, specimen, copy for imitation, etc.”, literally “what is taken out”); see exempt. Doublet of exemplum and sample. Displaced native Middle English forebisne, from Old English forebȳsn; and Middle English bisne, from Old English bȳsn (modern English bizen).

ex.en: For example, he speaks German, French and English.
ex.ja: たとえば、彼はドイツ語、フランス語、英語を話します。

ex.en: I like animals, for example, cats and dogs.
ex.ja: 例えば、猫や犬のような動物が好きです。

ex.en: She took a typical example of modern music.
ex.ja: 彼女は近代音楽の典型的な例を挙げた。

note.ja: ラテン語 exemplum（取り出されたもの）＝ ex（外へ）+ emere（取る）。全体から取り出した一つ →「例・手本」。sample も同じ語源。

en: The effect upon the judgment or feelings produced by any event, whether witnessed or participated in; personal and direct impressions as …
An activity one has performed.
To observe certain events; undergo a certain feeling or process; or perform certain actions that may alter one or contribute to one's kno…

experience.ety: From Middle English experience, from Old French, from Latin experientia (“a trial, proof, experiment, experimental knowledge, experience”), from experiens, present participle of experiri (“to try, put to the test, undertake, undergo”), from ex (“out”) + peritus (“experienced, expert”), past participle of *periri (“to go through”); see expert and peril. Displaced native Old English āfandung (“experience”) and āfandian (“to experience”).

ex.en: At last, they experienced the joy of victory.
ex.ja: ついに彼らは勝利の喜びを経験した。

ex.en: It was a very good experience for him.
ex.ja: それは彼にとってとてもいい経験だった。

ex.en: The story is based on his own experience.
ex.ja: その話は彼自身の体験に基づいている。

note.ja: ex（完全に）+ peri（試す）+ ence。試して身につけること →「経験（する）」。experiment（実験）、expert（試し尽くした人→専門家）も同じ。

en: To perceive sounds through the ear.
To perceive (a sound, or something producing a sound) with the ear, to recognize (something) in an auditory way.
you hear me

From Middle English har, heoren, her, here, heren, from Old English hēran, hīeran, hīran, hȳran (“to hear”), from Proto-West Germanic *hauʀijan, from Proto-Germanic *hauzijaną (“to hear”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ḱh₂owsyéti (“to be sharp-eared”), from *h₂eḱ- (“sharp”) + *h₂ows- (“ear”) + *-yéti (denominat

ex.en: Did you ever hear the like of it?
ex.ja: 君はそのようなことを聞いたことがあるか。

ex.en: I was glad to hear of your success.
ex.ja: 君の成功を聞いてうれしかった。

ex.en: I am glad to hear of your success.
ex.ja: 君の成功の知らせを聞いてうれしい。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「自然に耳に入る」。聞こえる（hear a noise）、耳にする（I heard that 〜）。listen は意識して耳を傾ける。

en: To come face to face with by accident; to encounter.
To come face to face with someone by arrangement.
A sports competition, especially for track and field or swimming.
A gathering of riders, horses and hounds for foxhunting; a field meet for hunting.

meet.ety:
From Middle English meten, from Old English mētan (“to meet, find, encounter”), from Proto-West Germanic *mōtijan (“to meet”), from Proto-Germanic *mōtijaną (“to meet”), from Proto-Indo-European *meh₂d- (“to come, meet”).
Cognates
Cognate with Scots met, mete, meit (“to meet”), North Frisian meet, mätje, möt (“to meet”), West Frisian mette, moetsje (“to meet”), Dutch ontmoeten (“to meet”), Low German möten (“to meet”), Danish møde (“to meet”), Elfdalian my̨öt (“to meet”), Faroese møta (“to meet”), Icelandic mæta (“to meet”), Norwegian Bokmål møte (“to meet”), Norwegian Nynorsk møta, møte (“to

ex.en: "Haven't we met somewhere before?" asked the student.
ex.ja: 「以前にどこかで会ったことがありませんか」とその学生はたずねた。

ex.en: You are not entitled to attend the meeting.
ex.ja: 君は会に出席する資格はない。

ex.en: Never did I dream of meeting you here.
ex.ja: 君にここで会おうとは夢にも思わなかった。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「出会って接点ができる」。会う（meet a friend）、出迎える（meet at the airport）、満たす（meet the needs ＝ 要求と接する）。

en: A set of structured activities; a plan of action.
A leaflet listing information about a play, game or other activity.
To enter a program or other instructions into (a computer or other electronic device) to instruct it to do a particular task.
To develop (software) by writing program code.

program.ety: Borrowed from French programme, from Late Latin programma (“a proclamation, edict”), from Ancient Greek πρόγραμμα (prógramma, “a written public notice, an edict”), from προγράφω (prográphō, “to set forth as a public notice”), from πρό (pró, “before”) + γράφω (gráphō, “to write”). Doublet of programma.

ex.en: Tell me about your program for the future.
ex.ja: 君の未来計画について話してください。

ex.en: At any rate, the program was a success.
ex.ja: とにかくそのプログラムは成功だった。

ex.en: TV programs have a bad influence on children.
ex.ja: テレビ番組が子供たちに悪い影響を与えている。

note.ja: pro（前もって）+ gram（書かれたもの）。前もって書いたもの →「予定表・計画・番組」。grammar（書き方の規則→文法）、telegram（遠くへ書く→電報）も同じ gram。

en: A grouping based on shared characteristics; a class.
classification of texts according to their literary style
To put text on paper using a typewriter.
To enter text or commands into a computer using a keyboard.

type.ety: From Middle English type (“symbol, figure, emblem”), from Latin typus, from Ancient Greek τύπος (túpos, “mark, impression, type”), from τύπτω (túptō, “to strike, beat”).

ex.en: This is an old type of American clock.
ex.ja: これは古い型のアメリカの時計です。

ex.en: This large type is easy on the eyes.
ex.ja: この大きな活字は眼に楽だ。

ex.en: These types of books have almost no value.
ex.ja: こういう種類の本はほとんど価値がない。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 typos（打った跡・型）から。型 →「種類・タイプ」、活字を打つ →「タイプする」。typical（典型的な）。

en: A very young human, particularly from birth to a couple of years old or until walking is fully mastered.
A very young human, even if not yet born.
Picked when small and immature (as in baby corn, baby potatoes).
Newest (overall, or in some group or state); most inexperienced.
To coddle; to pamper somebody like an infant.
To tend (something) with care; to be overly attentive to (something), fuss over.

From Middle English baby, babie (“baby”), a diminutive form of babe (“babe, baby”), equivalent to babe + -y/-ie (“endearing and diminutive suffix”). Perhaps ultimately imitative of baby talk (compare babble).

ex.en: What a cute baby! May I hold her?
ex.ja: まぁかわいい赤ちゃん私にも抱かせてくれますか。

ex.en: Look at a baby sleeping in the bed.
ex.ja: ベッドで眠っている赤ん坊を見なさい。

ex.en: The baby will be able to walk soon.
ex.ja: その赤ん坊はすぐに歩けるようになるでしょう。

note.ja: babe（赤ん坊）+ y。幼児の「バーバー」という声から生まれた語とされる。

en: An opportunity or possibility.
Random occurrence; luck.
Happening by chance, casual.
To try or risk.
To discover something by chance.

chance.ety: From Middle English chance, cheance, chaunce, cheaunce, a borrowing from Old French cheance (“accident, chance, luck”), from Vulgar Latin *cadentia (“falling”), from Latin cadere (“to fall, to die, to happen, occur”). Doublet of cadence and cadenza.

ex.en: You have a good chance to get well.
ex.ja: 君はよくなる見込みが十分ある。

ex.en: By chance, I met her in the street.
ex.ja: 偶然、私は道端で彼女に会った。

ex.en: Let's take a chance and go for broke.
ex.ja: 危険をおかして思いきってやってみよう。

note.ja: ラテン語 cadere（落ちる）から。cad（落ちる）。サイコロの落ち方 →「偶然・機会・見込み」。case、accident と同じ仲間。

en: A male parent, especially of a human; a male who parents a child (which he has sired, adopted, fostered, etc.).
A male ancestor more remote than a parent; a progenitor; especially, a first ancestor.
To be a father to; to sire.
To give rise to.

ex.ja: 海に面した部屋に変えてください。

ex.en: Let's go by train instead of by bus.
ex.ja: バスでなくて列車で行きましょう。

ex.en: I'd like to have tea instead of coffee.
ex.ja: コーヒーをやめて紅茶を頂きます。

note.ja: in + stead（場所）。その場所に →「その代わりに」。steady（しっかり立った）と同じ stead。

en: Of chief or leading importance; prime, principal.
Chief, most important, or principal in extent, size, or strength; consisting of the largest part.
To mainly play a specific character or side, or with specific equipment, during a game.
That which is chief or principal; the chief or main portion; the bulk, the greater part, gross.
The primary character that one plays in a video game in which one can play more than one character.

main.ety:
From Middle English mayn, main, maine, mæin, meyn, from main (noun) (see further at etymology 2); compare Old English mæġen (“strong, main, principal”) (used in combination) and Old Norse megn, megenn (“strong, main”).
The word is cognate with Old High German megīn (“strong, mighty”) (modern German Möge, Vermögen (“power, wealth”)), and also akin to Old English magan (“to be able to”). See also may.

ex.en: Hard work is the main element of success.
ex.ja: 勤勉は成功のための重要な要素だ。

ex.en: We are having fish for our main course.
ex.ja: メインディッシュを魚にしましたよ。

ex.en: Can you tell me where Main Street is?
ex.ja: メインストリートはどちらでしょうか。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「力のある・主な」。古英語 mægen（力）から。主要な、本管（water main）。might（力）と同じ祖先。

en: A particular point of space; a spot.
A particular point of time; an instant.

moment.ety: From Middle English moment, from Old French moment, from Latin mōmentum. Doublet of momentum and movement.

ex.ja: もうすぐここから逃げ出すのだ。

ex.en: Will you excuse me for just a moment?
ex.ja: ちょっと失礼してよいでしょうか。

ex.en: I want to see you for a moment.
ex.ja: ちょっと会いたいのだけれど。

note.ja: ラテン語 momentum（動き・はずみ）から。mov（動く）。わずかに動く間 →「瞬間」、物事を動かす重み →「重要性」。

en: A female parent, especially of a human; a female who parents a child (which she has given birth to, adopted, fostered, etc).
A pregnant female; mother-to-be; a female who gestates a baby.
To give birth to or produce (as its female parent) a child. (Compare father.)
To treat as a mother would be expected to treat her child; to nurture.

en: To appear; to look outwardly; to be perceived as.

ex.ja: 子供の頃は、周りのものが何でも大きく見えるものだ。

ex.ja: 君は何かほかのことを考えているみたいだね。

ex.ja: 君の考えは私の考えに似ているようだ。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「（外から見て）〜のようだ」。It seems that 〜（〜のようだ）。appear も近いが、seem は話し手の判断を表す。

fine.ety: From Middle English fin, fyn, from Old French fin (“fine, minute, exact”), of obscure origin, but probably derived from Latin fīnīre (“to finish”) or fīnis (“boundary, limit, end”), with an abstract sense of fine or thin also arising in many Romance languages (compare Italian, Portuguese, and Spanish fino). ex.ja: この部屋からの山の眺めは最高だ。

ex.ja: この天気は明日までもちますか。

ex.en: Nothing can force me to give it up.
ex.ja: 何も私にそれをあきらめるように強制することができない。

Offspring: one's natural child or children.

ex.ja: 少女達はその映画スターに夢中なっている。

en: A challenge, trial.
An examination, given often during the academic term.
To challenge, to put a strain on (something).
To refine (gold, silver, etc.) in a test or cupel; to subject to cupellation.

test.ety:
From Middle English test, teste, from Old French test, teste (“an earthen vessel, especially a pot in which metals were tried”), from Latin testum (“the lid of an earthen vessel, an earthen vessel, an earthen pot”), from *terstus, past participle of the root *tersa (“dry land”). See terra, thirst. The examination sense came via metaphor of the metallurgical sense: the way a metallurgist puts to the test their gold, a teacher may put to the test their students' knowledge.
Displaced Old English afandung.

ex.en: Ten to one you can pass the test.
ex.ja: 君がそのテストに合格することはまず間違いない。

ex.en: Don't worry about the result of the test.
ex.ja: テストの結果を心配するな。

ex.en: Don't worry about the result of your test.
ex.ja: テストの結果は気にするな。

note.ja: ラテン語 testum（土の壺）から。金属を試験する壺 →「試験・検査」。※ testify（証言する）の test（証人）とは別語源とされる。

en: The act of seeing or looking at something.
The range of vision.
To look at.
To regard in a stated way.

view.ety: From Middle English vewe, from Anglo-Norman vewe, from Old French veue f (French vue f), feminine past participle of veoir (“to see”) (French voir). Cognate with Italian vedere, as well as Portuguese and Spanish ver. Doublet of veduta and vista.

ex.ja: 危険を考慮して彼は後に残った。

ex.en: Look at this grand view of the ocean.
ex.ja: この雄大な海の眺めをごらんなさい。

ex.en: This room has fine view of the mountain.
ex.ja: この部屋からの山の眺めは最高だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 videre（見る）から。vid（見る）。見えるもの →「眺め・意見（物の見方）・見る」。review（見直す）、interview（互いに見る）も同じ。

en: The residents or inhabitants of Great Britain.
The citizens or inhabitants of the United Kingdom.
Of Britain.
Of the United Kingdom.

British.ety:
From Middle English Brittish, from Old English Brettisċ.
The spelling with single -t- appears in the 13th century under the influence of Medieval Latin Britannicus, but spelling with -tt- persists alongside -t- during the 13th to at least 18th centuries.
In reference to the island of Great Britain from ca. 1400 (Latin natio Anglica sive Britannica, Brittisshe occean 1398, the Britishe nacion 1548).
As a noun, referring to the British people, British soldiers, etc. from ca. 1600.

ex.en: This is an instance of modern British life.
ex.ja: これは英国の現代生活のほんの一例だ。

ex.en: Can you take us to the British Museum?
ex.ja: 大英博物館まで行ってくれますか。

ex.en: While in London, he visited the British Museum.
ex.ja: 彼はロンドンに滞在中に、大英博物館を訪れた。

note.ja: 古英語 Bryttisc から。ラテン語 Britto（ブリトン人）。Britain と同じ。

en: Relating to now, for the time being; current.
Located in the immediate vicinity.
The current moment or period of time.
The present tense.

ex.ja: 学生達が全員その授業に出席していたわけではない。

en: Of a person, regretful or apologetic for one's actions.
Of a person, grieved or saddened, especially by the loss of something or someone.
Expresses regret, remorse, or sorrow.
Said as a request to excuse one's unintentional behaviors.
The act of saying sorry; an apology.

ex.en: All right! You will be sorry for this.

A branch office of such an institution.

Not to be doubted or denied; established as a fact.
Having been determined but not specified.
Unnamed or undescribed members (of).

certain.ety: From Middle English certeyn, certein, certain, borrowed from Old French certain, from a Vulgar Latin unattested form *certānus, extended form of Latin certus (“fixed, resolved, certain”), of the same origin as cretus, past participle of cernere (“to separate, perceive, decide”). ex.en: I bought this ring at a certain place.
ex.ja: この指輪をある場所で買った。

ex.ja: ある程度彼を信用できる。

en: A Christian house of worship; a building where Christian religious services take place.
Christians collectively seen as a single spiritual community; Christianity; Christendom.
To conduct a religious service for (a woman after childbirth, or a newly married couple).
To educate someone religiously, as in a church.

Possibly from Proto-Germanic *kēgaz, *kēguz (“stake, post, pole”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵogʰ-, *ǵegʰ-, *ǵegʰn- (“branch, stake, bush”), which would make it cognate with Middle Low Ger

ex.en: Where was it that you found this key?
ex.ja: 君がこのかぎを見つけたのはどこでしたか。

ex.en: The boy was searching for the lost key.
ex.ja: その少年は無くした鍵を探していた。

ex.en: John took a key out of his pocket.
ex.ja: ジョンはポケットから鍵を取り出した。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「開けるための鍵」。鍵、（問題を解く）鍵・手がかり、重要な（key point）、（楽器の）鍵盤・調。

en: Mother.
used as a term of address for one's wife
To care for in a motherly way.

ex.en: I asked Mom to get some for you.
ex.ja: あなたのために、お母さんに買っておいてもらったの。

ex.en: My mom married my dad in the 80s.
ex.ja: おふくろはおやじと80年代に結婚したんだ。

ex.en: Mom, thank you for giving birth to me.
ex.ja: お母さん、産んでくれてありがとう。

note.ja: mother の幼児語。イギリスでは mum。

en: One of the many pieces of paper bound together within a book or similar document.
One side of a paper leaf in a bound document.
To mark or number the pages of, as a book or manuscript.
To turn several pages of a publication.

page.ety: Borrowed from Middle French page, from Latin pāgina, from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂ǵ-. Doublet of pagina.

ex.en: Please feel free to link to my page.
ex.ja: このページはリンクフリーです。

ex.en: The last page of this book is missing.
ex.ja: この本は最後の一枚が抜けている。

ex.en: That company just put up a web page.
ex.ja: あの会社もついにホームページを立ち上げたらしい。

note.ja: ラテン語 pagina（紙の1枚）から。→「ページ」。人を呼ぶ「呼び出す（page）」は宮廷の小姓（page）から。

en: A line or series of mountains, buildings, etc.
A fireplace; a fire or other cooking apparatus; now specifically, a large cooking stove with many burners (hotplates).
To travel over (an area, etc); to roam, wander.
To rove over or through.

range.ety: From Middle English rengen, from Old French rengier (“to range, to rank, to order”), from the noun renc, reng, ranc, rang (“a rank, row”), from Frankish *hring, from Proto-Germanic *hringaz (“ring, circle, curve”). Doublet of ring.

ex.en: What's the name of the mountain range?
ex.ja: あの山脈の名前は何と言いますか。

ex.en: I'm not moving out of range of that telephone.
ex.ja: 私はその電話の届く範囲より遠くに引っ越すわけではない。

ex.en: The students range in age from 18 to 25.
ex.ja: 生徒の年齢は１８歳から２５歳にわたっている。

note.ja: 古フランス語 rang（列）から。rank（列・階級）と同語源。並んだ範囲 →「範囲・山脈・（〜の範囲に）及ぶ」。

en: A second or subsequent reading of a text or artifact in an attempt to gain new insights.
An account intended as a critical evaluation of a text or a piece of work.
To survey; to look broadly over.
To write a critical evaluation of a new art work etc.; to write a review.

review.ety: From Middle English revewe, reveue, from Old French reveüe, revue (Modern French: revue), feminine form of reveü, past participle of reveoir (French: revoir), from Latin revideō, from re- +videō (“see, observe”) (English: video). Equivalent to re- + view. Compare retrospect. Doublet of revue.

ex.en: Did you try to review the English lessons?
ex.ja: 君は英語の復習をしようとしましたか。

ex.en: The educational system is now under review.
ex.ja: 今教育制度が見直されています。

ex.en: The New York Times reviews her gallery all the time.
ex.ja: ニューヨークタイムズは彼女のギャラリーにいつも取材にくるんだから。

note.ja: re（再び）+ view（見る）。もう一度見る →「見直し・復習・批評・審査」。

en: A particular discipline or branch of knowledge that is natural, measurable or consisting of systematic principles rather than intuition o…
Specifically the natural sciences.
To use science to solve a problem.

science.ety: From Middle English science, scyence, borrowed from Old French science, escience, from Latin scientia (“knowledge”), from sciēns, the present participle stem of scire (“to know”).

ex.en: Science has made rapid progress in this century.
ex.ja: 科学は今世紀になって急速な進歩を遂げた。

ex.en: Science begins when you ask why and how.
ex.ja: なぜ、どうして、と問いかけるときから科学は始まる。

ex.en: You find that it is shaped by science.
ex.ja: それが科学によって形作られていることが分かる。

note.ja: sci（知る）+ ence。知ること →「知識」→「科学」。conscious（共に知っている→意識している）も同じ sci。

en: The buying and selling of goods and services on a market.
A particular instance of buying or selling, or a series of related transactions executed as a single investment.
To engage in trade.
To be traded at a certain price or under certain conditions.
Of a product, produced for sale in the ordinary bulk retail trade and hence of only the most basic quality.

Displaced Middle English chaffare.

ex.ja: 日本はイギリスと多くの貿易をしている。

ex.en: Japan does a lot of trade with Canada.
ex.ja: 日本はカナダとの貿易が盛んだ。

ex.en: Japan has a lot of trade with Canada.
ex.ja: 日本はカナダと大量の貿易をしている。

note.ja: tread（踏む）と同じ祖先。踏み固められた道 →（商売の道）→「貿易・取引・商売・職業」。

ex.ja: 君は彼を偉大だとおもってはならない。

ex.en: How did you hit upon such an idea?
ex.ja: そんなアイディアをどのようにして思い付いたのですか。

ex.en: It has an important influence upon our lives.
ex.ja: それは我々の生活に重大な影響を及ぼす。

en: More than one (of an indeterminate set of things).
Having a broad range (of different elements).

various.ety: Borrowed from Middle French varieux, from Latin varius (“manifold, diverse, various, parti-colored, variegated, also changing, changeable, fickle, etc.”). By surface analysis, vary + -ous.

ex.en: We can apply the discovery to various uses.
ex.ja: その発見はいろいろな用途に応用できる。

ex.en: Wood is made into various kinds of articles.
ex.ja: 木からはいろんな物が作られる。

ex.en: We studied Greek culture from various aspects.
ex.ja: 我々はギリシャ文化をいろいろな見地から研究した。

note.ja: ラテン語 varius（まだらの・さまざまな）から。→「さまざまな・いろいろな」。vary（変わる）、variety（多様性）。

en: Mental focus.
An action or remark expressing concern for or interest in someone or something, especially romantic interest.
Used as a command to bring soldiers to the attention position.
A call for people to be quiet/stop doing what they are presently doing and pay heed to what they are to be told or shown.

ex.ja: 君は君の幸福に注意を払うべきだ。

ex.ja: もう少し注意すべきだった。

ex.ja: その子は病院で適切な医療を受ける必要がある。

en: Son of the same parents as another person.
A male having at least one parent in common with another person (see half-brother, stepbrother).
To treat as a brother.
Expressing exasperation.

ex.ja: ビルと彼の弟と全然区別がつかない。

en: A being involved in the action of a story; a persona.
A distinguishing feature; characteristic; trait; nature; phene.

ex.ja: その問題は新しい性格を帯び始めた。

ex.en: The problem began to assume an international character.
ex.ja: その問題は国際的な性格のものとなり始めた。

ex.en: I regard him as a man of character.
ex.ja: 私は彼のことを人格者とみなしている。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 kharaktēr（刻み込まれた印）から。刻まれた特徴 →「性格・特徴・登場人物・文字」。

Headship, the status of being a chief or leader.
Primary; principal.
Intimate, friendly.

ex.ja: 彼は警察署長です。

ex.ja: テレビでフットボールの試合を見るのは楽しかった。
